_comment: Mutation testing — does the suite NOTICE when working code is broken?
Coverage says which lines ran. It cannot say whether anything would have
complained. A repo-wide audit measured that gap by hand: 20 semantic
mutations, 12 initially killed. This automates the same question so it
stops depending on someone remembering to ask it.
The scope is the operator's security guards, the approval logic behind
them, and the version comparison the update banner is built on. Widening
it is not free and not always possible — read the notes below before
adding anything. Three things are excluded from the scope on purpose:
system-prompt.ts and api-client.ts (both argued under `mutate`), and
static mutants (argued under `ignoreStatic`). Two of the three were
decided by measurement; the system-prompt one is a judgement about prose.
_mutate_comment: system-prompt.ts — 59% of that file is English prose inside template
literals: the instructions handed to the model. Stryker cheerfully mutates
that prose, and the only test that could kill such a mutant is one pinning
the exact wording, which would then fail on every legitimate edit to the
prompt. Those are mutants you do not want killed. Its actual logic (which
preamble goes with which scope) is three one-line functions with unit
api-client.ts — the cost is quadratic in the wrong variable. 75 modules
import it, 40 of them in src/lib/api, so virtually every component test
executes it: each of its ~120 mutants replays a large share of the 4,349
tests. Measured, it alone projected ~10 of an 11-hour run, for mutants
that broad incidental coverage would mostly kill by accident rather than
by design. It keeps its own unit tests (src/pages/__tests__/
api-client.test.tsx); it does not get this gate.
The rule the two share: mutation testing pays off on code with FOCUSED
tests. Every file below has 1-5 importers. Check that before widening.
_ignorePatterns_comment: Stryker does NOT read .gitignore. It walks the working directory and copies
what it finds into a sandbox PER TEST RUNNER — four of them by default — so
anything large and irrelevant is copied four times before a single mutant
`.claude` matters most for anyone running this from the main checkout
rather than a worktree: `.claude/worktrees/` holds full checkouts of other
branches. Vitest already excludes it from test collection for the same
NOT excluded, and it looks like it should be: `.design-sync`. It is 145 KB
of config that appears to have nothing to do with the tests, but
`.design-sync/config.json` off disk — drop it from the sandbox and that
test fails inside the dry run, which reads as 'your suite is broken'
rather than 'your sandbox is missing a file'.
_ignoreStatic_comment: A 'static' mutant sits in code that runs at module load — a top-level
const, an array literal built once at import. Stryker cannot swap one in
without reloading the module, so it restarts the runner and replays the
ENTIRE suite for each one. Measured on the first attempt: 223 static
mutants, 14% of the total, holding 98% of the projected runtime.
So they are skipped, and the honest cost is stated plainly: the score
below covers behaviour, not the values of module-level constants. If you
add a security-relevant constant (an allow-list, a scope table), a unit
test asserting its contents is the thing that guards it — this gate will
_dryRunTimeout_comment: Stryker runs the WHOLE suite once up front, instrumented, to learn which
tests touch which code. For this scope that is 1,537 tests in ~11 minutes.
The cost is not fixed — it tracks how widely the mutated files are imported.
With api-client.ts in scope the same step pulled in 4,349 tests and took
16m54s and 26m08s on two runs of the identical config, which is the other
half of why that file is excluded above.
Not worked around by pointing Stryker at a subset of TEST files: with
perTest coverage the per-mutant runs already execute only the handful of
tests that reach the mutant, so trimming buys nothing after this step — it
only risks reporting a mutant as survived because the test that would have
caught it was hidden, and a gate that cries wolf gets deleted.
30, not the 5-minute default it blew through on the first attempt, and not
11: CI runners are slower, and the spread between two identical local runs
_thresholds_comment: A ratchet, in the shape check-i18n.mjs already uses for its COLLIDING set:
`break` is the floor CI enforces. Raise it when the real score rises; never
lower it to make a build pass — a drop means a test stopped noticing
something that it used to notice.
Measured 84.29% over 1,375 mutants at the time this landed (81.89% before
the three files the first run caught untested). 82 leaves ~2 points for
jitter: 8 mutants time out rather than being killed outright, and a timeout
counts as detected, so a slower or faster runner moves the total slightly.
